title: Unassuming beauty
caption: A star field in Crux, the Southern Cross, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Stars of every age crowd this image from ESO's Very Large Telescope, some close by in the foreground and others far in the distance. Their distinct red and blue hues come from the way the picture was made. The patch of sky lies in Crux, the Southern Cross, an extremely bright stretch of the Milky Way.

Astronomical cameras record light in shades of gray, so color pictures like this are built from several images taken through different filters, each letting through a particular range of wavelengths. Each filtered image is given its own color, and the separate images are then combined. The result represents the different wavelengths of light in color.

The picture was taken with the FORS instrument, short for FOcal Reducer and low dispersion Spectrograph. It was made for the ESO Cosmic Gems program, which produces images of interesting or attractive objects for education and public outreach.

understand.summary: The FORS2 instrument on the Very Large Telescope imaged this field through blue, visual, red and hydrogen-alpha filters, each assigned its own color before combining. The source does not publish which color was given to each filter.
filters: 440 nm · Optical b (Very Large Telescope FORS2)
557 nm · Optical v (Very Large Telescope FORS2)
655 nm · Optical R (Very Large Telescope FORS2)
660 nm · Optical H-alpha (Very Large Telescope FORS2)
understand.eye: The colors come from filters and processing choices, and the telescope's exposures reveal far more distant, faint stars than the eye could see.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Cosmic Gems runs on telescope time that is unsuitable for scientific work. Even so, the data may be scientifically useful, so they are made available to astronomers through ESO's science archive.
alt: A field of red and blue stars at various distances.
